quote: I'm not I'm just trying to find out about this stuff.
stewart_read: Customer handed the rep an open door to ask what interested him in solar — a vague, low-commitment framing that needed probing.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this line as noise rather than an anchor opportunity worth probing given the customer's brisk tone.
coaching_implication: Interest question was skipped entirely per verified events; this line was the natural entry point to ask it.

quote: I know that one at a time is more. But I'd say, like, $2.50 average.
stewart_read: Bill figure captured but rep immediately moved to the next verify item with a flat 'Okay' instead of reflecting it back.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be sequencing verify items strictly script-order and planning to use the bill later at booking — but no later reference occurs.
coaching_implication: Should acknowledge the bill pain in the moment ("that's a big bill to be paying every month") to start building alignment against the utility.

quote: Why do you need it all about it?
stewart_read: This is a trust/privacy objection about the bill request; rep gave a factual explanation (kWh graph) rather than a flip, but it did work.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep just explained rather than resolving suspicion at the trust level. Strategic read is not supported — no reassurance language ('no obligation') was used.
coaching_implication: A brief reassurance ('just so our design team sizes the system right, no other reason') would land faster than the technical explanation alone.

coaching_implication: Good adaptive move; document as a valid alternative path for app-based utility accounts.
